keep: The idea is named up front: near full, the spare current splits water into hydrogen and oxygen, and the room's air is sized from the charger's largest fault current.

One picture carries the lesson: the battery room with the current slider up to the example 20 A fault current, the cell stepper, the room switch, the real opening against the dashed required opening drawn to scale, air at an example 0.1 m/s, and the hydrogen readout against the cited bands at 0.4, 1 and 4 per cent.

Worked numbers from the rule: 0.3 × 24 × 20 × 10 = 1440 cm², 576 cm² in an enclosure, 36 cm² from a 0.5 A float (forty times too small), 14.4 L/s at 0.1 m/s, 0.4 doubling to 0.8 per cent with half the opening, and 1650 cm² and 16.5 L/s for 55 cells at 10 A.
The readout is honest: HSE's rule read backwards, 4 ÷ S per cent at the required opening, so 1.2 × N × I ÷ opening, called a model of a well-mixed room.

Each named slip has a DO screen with a hint per wrong pick: 4 per cent as the working limit (3), S upside down (5), float current used as I (7), the same gas in less air (9), sealed means gas-free (11), and a stopped fan (13).
Recall opener from Heat and fluids lesson 6 (0.5 m² at 2 m/s), as the brief asks; area × speed is used, not retaught.
fix: Causal step skipped: why the opening is multiplied by N. Say each cell in the string carries the same current, so each makes the same gas, and N cells make N times as much.

False absolute in screen 7's hint for 'none': 'most of it splits water' is not true of a full battery on float. Say a full battery still takes current if the charger pushes it, and that spare current splits water.
False absolute: 'Real gas mixes unevenly' in explain. Say real gas may mix unevenly.
The fan appears with no introduction. Say the outlet carries a fan, that the model moves air at 0.1 m/s by fan or draught alike, and that the switch is 'Fan fails'.
Colon chain: 'S is the dilution factor: 10 for … and 4 for …'. Split it into two sentences.
Practice's 'Gas comes fastest at and past full charge' sits on the safety step; keep it, but name boost and equalise as the hard charges so the step reads on its own.

shape.ruleInWords: yes: each opening at least 0.3 × N × I × S cm², I the charger's fault current, S 10 where people enter and 4 for an enclosure; hydrogen is the gas spread through the air, flow = area × speed
shape.workedExampleWithRealNumbers: yes (24 cells, 20 A: 1440 cm² and 14.4 L/s; 55 cells, 10 A: 1650 cm² and 16.5 L/s)
shape.misconceptionShownFailing: yes: float current as I (7), sealed means gas-free (11), 4 per cent as the limit (3), S upside down (5)
shape.analogyWithBreaks: yes: the protective conductor sized for fault current, not load; breaks because a circuit fault clears in a fraction of a second while a charger fault can run for hours
shape.putItIntoPractice: yes: ventilation check first, steps, rule of thumb, worked example, mistakes
